9474.title: Kalman Filter
9474.heading: Kalman Filter
9474.content:
A Kalman filter is a Bayesian filter specialized to linear state transitions and observations with Gaussian uncertainty. Those assumptions allow the belief state to be represented by a mean and covariance and updated analytically.

The prediction step propagates both the estimate and its uncertainty, while the correction step balances that prediction against a measurement. The relative covariances determine how strongly each source influences the posterior.

Labels, units, rounding, and captions should be chosen deliberately instead of exposing raw object names.

9489.heading: K-Nearest Neighbors
9489.content:
K-nearest neighbors predicts from the labels or outcomes of the $k$ training observations closest to a new point. For classification, the local class proportions estimate conditional probabilities and the majority supplies the predicted label.

Small $k$ creates a flexible, variable boundary, while large $k$ smooths across broader neighborhoods and can hide local structure. Feature scale and [[Dimension Reduction]] affect which observations count as nearby.

9492.heading: K-Nearest Neighbor Outlier
9492.content:
A K-nearest-neighbor outlier has an unusually large distance to its kth nearest neighbor or an unusually large sum of distances to its k nearest neighbors. The score ranks observations by local isolation.

The choice of k defines the neighborhood scale. Computing all pairwise distances is expensive, so randomized ordering and pruning can reduce work.

9495.content:
K-means initialization sensitivity is the dependence of the final partition on its starting seeds or assignments. Different starts can change the convergence path, produce empty groups, and settle at different local minima.

An analysis should use deliberate seeding or multiple runs and report how stable the solution is. A single unexplained start gives weak evidence for the resulting clusters.

9498.content:
K-means convergence occurs when an allocation pass causes no material membership or centroid changes, or when improvement falls below a tolerance. At that point the objective cannot be improved by the algorithm's current local update rule.

Convergence establishes stability of one run, not global optimality. A different initialization can converge to a different partition with a better or worse objective value.

9501.content:
A k-gram sequence feature represents an ordered contiguous pattern of exactly k elements. Its value may indicate presence, count occurrences, or weight the pattern within a sequence.

Increasing k captures more context but expands the candidate space and makes individual patterns rarer. Support constraints and feature selection help control this combinatorial growth.

9504.title: K-Means Clustering
9504.heading: K-Means Clustering
9504.content:
K-means clustering partitions multidimensional data by repeatedly assigning each point to its nearest centroid and recomputing centroids from the assigned points. Distance calculations and centroid aggregation continue until a stopping condition is met.

At scale, points can remain cached on distributed workers while partial centroid sums are combined through [[Collective Communication]]. Its repeated structure makes K-means a useful benchmark for [[Iterative Data Processing]].

The source distinguishes update variants: MacQueen updates centroids after each reallocation, while Forgy holds seeds fixed for a full allocation pass and then recomputes centers. All can converge to a local optimum determined by the initial partition, so repeated starts and comparison of final squared-error values are part of responsible use.

Making a prediction at commit time supports rapid review and testing. The representation must use only information available then and distinguish risky complexity from ordinary large or experienced changes.

Judgmental analysis captures how individual judges combine predictor information and then groups judges whose decision equations are similar. Each judge's ratings are modeled with multiple regression, and a hierarchical procedure merges policies while tracking the loss of predictive efficiency.

The method produces both interpretable policy equations and evidence about agreement. It can identify several policy groups or, when supported, a combined consensus policy.

9516.heading: JSON Web Token
9516.content:
A JSON Web Token is a compact token format used to carry signed claims between an issuer and a client or API. Its signature allows the recipient to detect alteration and validate the issuing authority.

In a single-page application, IdentityServer can issue a JWT after authentication and the client can present it on API requests. The token is evidence to validate, not permission by itself; [[Authorization]] still evaluates the claims against an operation's policy.

9519.title: JSX
9519.heading: JSX
9519.content:
JSX is a syntax extension that lets a React component describe element structure with HTML-like expressions inside JavaScript or TypeScript. A build step transforms JSX into ordinary JavaScript calls that create React elements.

Expressions in braces can supply values, conditions, attributes, and repeated children. JSX is not sent to the browser unchanged; it is authoring syntax for producing the [[React Element|element]] tree.

9522.title: JSON Serialization
9522.heading: JSON Serialization
9522.content:
JSON serialization converts application data into a language-independent text representation that can be placed in an [[HTTP Response]]. Deserialization performs the reverse transformation so a typed client or server object can represent the received values.

An ASP.NET Core endpoint can serialize health or entity results, and an Angular client can consume the same structure through [[Angular HttpClient]]. Naming conventions must agree across the boundary or be configured explicitly.

The Azure projects serialize work items, queue messages, cognitive-service responses, and bot configuration at system boundaries. The bot chapter also uses the .NET Core 3 `JsonDocument` API to select an intent's response array from an embedded JSON resource without constructing a larger object model.

9525.title: JPEG Thumbnail Consistency
9525.heading: JPEG Thumbnail Consistency
9525.content:
JPEG thumbnail consistency compares an embedded preview with the thumbnail that the claimed camera would be expected to generate from the full-resolution image. The comparison considers visible content as well as dimensions, sharpening, resampling, and compression characteristics.

A leftover preview can expose an edit directly, while an unusually regenerated preview can reveal that other software resaved the file. A consistent pair cannot establish authenticity because an editor can update both representations or remove the thumbnail entirely.

9528.title: JPEG Signature
9528.heading: JPEG Signature
9528.content:
A JPEG signature is a collection of encoding choices that can characterize a camera or software pipeline. Quantization tables, embedded-thumbnail properties, and the order and contents of marker segments are particularly useful because different devices and applications package JPEG data differently.

A mismatch between a file's signature and its claimed source suggests that the image was resaved or did not come directly from that pipeline. A match is not proof of origin, since signatures can be shared, copied, or changed by firmware and export settings.

9530.sourceSearchName: jpeg recompression probe jpeg recompression probe
9530.title: JPEG Recompression Probe
9530.heading: Document

9531.sourceSearchName: jpeg recompression probe jpeg recompression probe
9531.title: JPEG Recompression Probe
9531.heading: JPEG Recompression Probe
9531.content:
A JPEG recompression probe repeatedly saves a test image at candidate quality settings and measures the pixel difference between each result and the original file. A region previously encoded at one of those settings can show an anomalously small or structured difference near the matching quality.

Comparing the difference maps across qualities is the operational basis of [[JPEG Ghost]] analysis. The probe must preserve relevant alignment and encoding conditions, and it should be treated as a test of compression history rather than direct proof of compositing.

9534.sourceSearchName: jpeg marker packaging jpeg marker packaging
9534.title: JPEG Marker Packaging
9534.heading: JPEG Marker Packaging
9534.content:
JPEG marker packaging is the arrangement of segments that identify image parameters, quantization and coding tables, metadata, scan data, and the file's beginning and end. The standard permits flexibility, so cameras and editing applications often emit recognizable marker orders and payload conventions.

When software opens and resaves a photograph, it may reconstruct this packaging even if the visible pixels change little. Comparing the structure with reference files can therefore reveal an unexpected encoder, though firmware versions and export options can produce legitimate variation.

9537.sourceSearchName: jpeg quantization table signature jpeg quantization table signature
9537.title: JPEG Quantization Table Signature
9537.heading: JPEG Quantization Table Signature
9537.content:
A JPEG quantization table signature uses the values that control how strongly spatial-frequency coefficients are rounded during compression. A color JPEG can contain three 8-by-8 tables—one for luminance and two for chrominance—providing 192 values whose pattern may be distinctive to a device or application.

Comparing those values with known outputs can identify an incompatible encoder or prior resave. Attribution remains probabilistic because different products can share tables and some cameras select tables dynamically according to scene or quality settings.

9538.sourceSearchName: jpeg quantization table signature jpeg quantization table signature
9538.title: JPEG Quantization Table Signature
9538.heading: References

9540.title: JPEG Ghost
9540.heading: JPEG Ghost
9540.content:
A JPEG ghost is a regional difference pattern that appears when an already compressed image is recompressed across a range of candidate qualities. Pixels originating from a previous JPEG save respond differently near their earlier quality level than pixels with another compression history.

Mapping average absolute differences can reveal a pasted region whose effective quality differs from its surroundings. The result indicates inconsistent prior compression, not the exact editing operation, and naturally mixed or repeatedly processed files can complicate interpretation.

9542.sourceSearchName: jpeg encoding pipeline jpeg encoding pipeline
9542.title: JPEG Encoding Pipeline
9542.heading: Document

9543.sourceSearchName: jpeg encoding pipeline jpeg encoding pipeline
9543.title: JPEG Encoding Pipeline
9543.heading: JPEG Encoding Pipeline
9543.content:
The JPEG encoding pipeline first converts RGB pixels to luminance and chrominance channels and may downsample the color channels. It centers the values, divides each channel into 8-by-8 blocks, and applies a discrete cosine transform to express every block as spatial-frequency coefficients.

Frequency-dependent quantization performs the lossy step by rounding those coefficients. Zigzag ordering, run-length representation, and Huffman coding then exploit the many resulting zeros and repeated symbols without adding further loss. The chosen tables and packaging help form a [[JPEG Signature]].

9544.sourceSearchName: jpeg encoding pipeline jpeg encoding pipeline
9544.title: JPEG Encoding Pipeline
9544.heading: References

9545.sourceSearchName: jpeg decoding pipeline jpeg decoding pipeline
9545.title: JPEG Decoding Pipeline
9545.heading: Document

9546.sourceSearchName: jpeg decoding pipeline jpeg decoding pipeline
9546.title: JPEG Decoding Pipeline
9546.heading: JPEG Decoding Pipeline
9546.content:
The JPEG decoding pipeline reverses the lossless coding steps, restores quantized frequency coefficients, applies the inverse discrete cosine transform to each block, and converts luminance and chrominance data back into displayed color pixels.

It cannot undo the rounding performed during encoding. Missing coefficients are estimated only through the stored quantized values, which is why successive saves can accumulate distortion and why prior quantization may remain detectable after a second compression.

9547.sourceSearchName: jpeg decoding pipeline jpeg decoding pipeline
9547.title: JPEG Decoding Pipeline
9547.heading: References

9549.title: JPEG Compression
9549.heading: JPEG Compression
9549.content:
JPEG compression reduces image storage by preserving visual information to which people are more sensitive and discarding less noticeable detail. It represents brightness and color separately, transforms small pixel blocks into spatial frequencies, quantizes those coefficients, and encodes the resulting values compactly.

The scheme is lossy: lower quality produces smaller files but greater distortion. Because its block structure and quantization leave predictable traces, JPEG is both a source of ordinary artifacts and a record of encoding history used by forensic methods.

9551.sourceSearchName: jpeg compression artifact jpeg compression artifact
9551.title: JPEG Compression Artifact
9551.heading: Document

9552.sourceSearchName: jpeg compression artifact jpeg compression artifact
9552.title: JPEG Compression Artifact
9552.heading: JPEG Compression Artifact
9552.content:
A JPEG compression artifact is visible distortion caused by blockwise transformation, chroma reduction, and coefficient quantization rather than by scene content. Strong compression can create 8-by-8 blocking, ringing around sharp edges, color smearing, and loss of fine texture.

These patterns are often mistaken for evidence of editing. A forensic analyst should first determine whether an alleged anomaly is a normal consequence of the file's quality and repeated saves; only spatially or historically inconsistent artifacts support a tampering hypothesis.

9553.sourceSearchName: jpeg compression artifact jpeg compression artifact
9553.title: JPEG Compression Artifact
9553.heading: References

9555.title: Journal Table 1
9555.heading: Journal Table 1
9555.content:
A journal Table 1 summarizes the analytic sample and the distribution of exposures and candidate confounders. For a categorical outcome it commonly reports frequencies and proportions overall and by outcome group; for a continuous outcome it commonly adds group means and standard deviations.

Bivariate test results may help readers understand group differences. The table should be generated from analysis objects or structured data whenever possible, because manually copying values from console output into a spreadsheet creates avoidable transcription risk.

9558.title: Joule Heating
9558.heading: Joule Heating
9558.content: Joule heating is heat produced when current flows through electrical resistance. Its rate is $Q=I^2R$, so raising current increases this loss quickly. Unlike the reversible [[Peltier Effect]] or [[Thomson Effect]], resistance heating does not change into cooling when current direction reverses. In a [[Thermoelectric Generator]], it subtracts from the temperature-difference energy available for useful output.

9560.sourceSearchName: joint probability distribution joint probability distribution
9560.title: Joint Probability Distribution
9560.heading: Document

9561.sourceSearchName: joint probability distribution joint probability distribution
9561.title: Joint Probability Distribution
9561.heading: Joint Probability Distribution
9561.content:
A joint probability distribution assigns probabilities to combinations of values across several variables. It represents every probabilistic relationship the description makes available and is normalized over the full joint state space.

Bayesian programs rarely store an unrestricted joint table. They decompose it into smaller conditional factors using justified independence assumptions, then reconstruct the terms required for a particular question.

9579.heading: Jancey's K-Means Method
9579.content:
Jancey's K-means method assigns observations to the nearest class point, then obtains each new class point by reflecting the old point through the new cluster centroid. Passes continue until moving observations no longer improves the solution.

The method implicitly minimizes a within-cluster error function. Like other K-means variants, it can require several initial configurations to explore alternative local optima.

Jasmine is a JavaScript testing framework used to define test suites, setup, individual specifications, and expectations. Angular component tests use its functions to describe behavior and assert rendered or component state.

Jasmine defines the tests, while [[Karma]] runs them in a browser environment and reports their combined results.

9585.heading: Jacquard Punched-Card Control
9585.content:
The Jacquard loom used chains of punched cards to determine which threads were lifted on each line of a woven pattern. Its physical card sequence acted as external, replaceable control information for the machine.

This separation between mechanism and instructions anticipated [[Software]]. Changing the card deck changed the produced pattern without rebuilding the loom.

9588.title: Jacobson Radical
9588.heading: Jacobson Radical
9588.content:
The Jacobson radical of a ring is the intersection of all its [[Maximal Ideal]]s. An element a belongs to it exactly when 1 − ab is a [[Ring Unit]] for every ring element b.

The Jacobson radical controls finite generation through [[Nakayama's Lemma]]. In a [[Local Ring]], it is simply the unique maximal ideal.

9591.title: Jacobi Method
9591.heading: Jacobi Method
9591.content:
The Jacobi method rearranges each equation of a [[Linear System]] to solve for one unknown, then computes every component of the next approximation using only values from the previous iteration.

Because its updates are simultaneous, it is simple but may converge slowly or diverge. [[Strict Diagonal Dominance]] is a useful sufficient condition for convergence.

9594.sourceSearchName: jacobi eigenvalue algorithm jacobi eigenvalue algorithm
9594.title: Jacobi Eigenvalue Algorithm
9594.heading: Jacobi Eigenvalue Algorithm
9594.content:
The Jacobi eigenvalue algorithm repeatedly applies plane rotations to a real [[Symmetric Matrix]] to eliminate off-diagonal entries.

Each step produces an orthogonally similar matrix, preserving eigenvalues while moving the matrix toward diagonal form. The accumulated rotations also produce the eigenvectors.

9597.sourceSearchName: jack kilby integrated circuit jack kilby integrated circuit
9597.title: Jack Kilby Integrated Circuit
9597.heading: Jack Kilby Integrated Circuit
9597.content:
Jack Kilby demonstrated at Texas Instruments that all components of a circuit could be made from semiconductor material. His 1958 oscillator used a single germanium wafer, with fine wires connecting its elements.

The experiment established the integrated-circuit concept. Its wiring method was less suited to mass production than the planar approach developed soon afterward in California.

9600.title: Jaccard Index
9600.heading: Jaccard Index
9600.content:
The Jaccard index for clustering compares the number of observation pairs placed together in both partitions with the number placed together in at least one. Pairs separated by both solutions do not increase the score.

This focus on shared positive membership can be useful when co-clustering is more informative than mutual separation. The value ranges from no shared pairs to identical positive assignments.

9603.title: Iterative Refinement
9603.heading: Iterative Refinement
9603.content:
Iterative refinement improves an approximate solution $x^{(k)}$ by computing the residual $r=b-Ax^{(k)}$, solving $Ay=r$ for a correction, and setting $x^{(k+1)}=x^{(k)}+y$.

The same coefficient matrix is reused. A few correction steps can recover accuracy lost while solving an [[Ill-Conditioned Linear System]], provided the residual is computed accurately enough.

9605.sourceSearchName: iterative partition clustering iterative partition clustering
9605.title: Iterative Partition Clustering
9605.heading: Document

9606.sourceSearchName: iterative partition clustering iterative partition clustering
9606.title: Iterative Partition Clustering
9606.heading: Iterative Partition Clustering
9606.content:
Iterative partition clustering alternates between assigning observations to groups and updating group representatives. A pass continues until no beneficial reallocation remains or another convergence rule is satisfied.

The procedure searches a large space through local improvements. Repeating it from distinct initial partitions helps reveal sensitivity and can produce a better final objective value.

9609.sourceSearchName: iterative linear solver iterative linear solver
9609.title: Iterative Linear Solver
9609.heading: Iterative Linear Solver
9609.content:
An iterative linear solver begins with an approximate vector and repeatedly applies an update intended to approach the solution of $Ax=b$. It produces usable approximations before exact arithmetic would finish.

These methods are attractive for large [[Sparse Matrix|sparse matrices]], where direct elimination may require excessive work or destroy sparsity. Convergence depends on the coefficient matrix and the chosen iteration.

9612.title: Iterative Development
9612.heading: Iterative Development
9612.content:
Iterative development revisits a product repeatedly, using what each working version teaches to revise its design. Each iteration contains a small pass through analysis, design, implementation, integration, and testing instead of assigning those activities to one long sequence.

For games, this converts uncertainty about feasibility and fun into evidence through a playable build. Iteration is therefore a learning structure as well as a delivery cadence.

9614.sourceSearchName: iterative data processing iterative data processing
9614.title: Iterative Data Processing
9614.heading: Document

9615.sourceSearchName: iterative data processing iterative data processing
9615.title: Iterative Data Processing
9615.heading: Iterative Data Processing
9615.content:
Iterative data processing repeats a computation until a convergence rule or iteration limit is reached. Clustering, graph ranking, linear algebra, and expectation-maximization often reuse the same large inputs during every round.

Launching separate MapReduce jobs for each round adds disk and process overhead. Loop-aware runtimes can cache invariant data, keep workers alive, and exchange only the partial results needed for the next update.

9616.title: Iterative Data Processing
9616.heading: References

9617.sourceSearchName: iterative classification algorithm iterative classification algorithm
9617.title: Iterative Classification Algorithm
9617.heading: Document

9618.sourceSearchName: iterative classification algorithm iterative classification algorithm
9618.title: Iterative Classification Algorithm
9618.heading: Iterative Classification Algorithm
9618.content:
An iterative classification algorithm for networks alternates between predicting node labels and rebuilding relational features from the current predictions of neighboring nodes. Initial labels usually come from a classifier using only local attributes.

Iteration lets mutually dependent predictions reinforce one another until a stopping condition is reached. It can also amplify an early mistake, so confidence controls, update ordering, and convergence behavior matter.

9619.title: Iterative Classification Algorithm
9619.heading: References

9620.sourceSearchName: iterative convergence criterion iterative convergence criterion
9620.title: Iterative Convergence Criterion
9620.heading: Document

9621.sourceSearchName: iterative convergence criterion iterative convergence criterion
9621.title: Iterative Convergence Criterion
9621.heading: Iterative Convergence Criterion
9621.content:
An iterative convergence criterion determines when an approximation process should stop or whether it will approach the desired solution. A practical rule compares successive approximations or the residual against a chosen tolerance.

A theoretical criterion may use the [[Spectral Radius]] or a norm of the [[Iteration Matrix]]. Small step-to-step change should be interpreted with care because it does not always guarantee a small solution error.

9622.title: Iterative Convergence Criterion
9622.heading: References

9624.title: Iteration Matrix
9624.heading: Iteration Matrix
9624.content:
An iteration matrix expresses a linear update as $x^{(k+1)}=Tx^{(k)}+c$. The error after successive steps is controlled by powers of $T$.

A stationary iteration converges for every starting vector when the [[Spectral Radius]] of $T$ is less than one. Matrix norms can provide easier sufficient tests.

9627.title: Iteration Time
9627.heading: Iteration Time
9627.content:
Iteration time is the delay between making a change and receiving useful evidence about its effect. Compilation, asset processing, approval, integration, testing, and defect correction can all lengthen this loop.

Measuring the whole delay prevents teams from optimizing one fast step while ignoring waiting elsewhere. Shorter iteration time allows more design learning within the same calendar period.

9629.sourceSearchName: iteration control structure iteration control structure
9629.title: Iteration Control Structure
9629.heading: Document

9630.sourceSearchName: iteration control structure iteration control structure
9630.title: Iteration Control Structure
9630.heading: Iteration Control Structure
9630.content:
An iteration control structure repeats a sequence of steps while a continuation condition holds or until a stopping condition is reached. It is also called a loop.

Iteration lets an [[Algorithm]] apply the same operation to successive data or progressively improve a result. Its condition must support [[Algorithm Termination]]; otherwise the procedure can enter an infinite loop and fail to produce its intended output.

9631.sourceSearchName: iteration control structure iteration control structure
9631.title: Iteration Control Structure
9631.heading: References

9633.title: Itemset
9633.heading: Itemset
9633.content:
An itemset is a finite set of items considered together in a transaction database. Its occurrence is counted in every transaction containing all of its members.

Frequent itemsets provide the candidates from which association rules are derived. The number of possible itemsets grows exponentially with the number of distinct items.

9636.title: Iteration Cadence
9636.heading: Iteration Cadence
9636.content:
Iteration cadence is the rate at which a team can turn a design question into a prototype, observe play, evaluate evidence, and try a revision. A short cadence exposes mistaken assumptions before they accumulate dependencies and sunk cost.

Speed does not mean skipping reflection. The cycle remains useful only when each pass records its question, evidence, and decision well enough for the next pass to build on what was learned.

9639.title: Itemset Support
9639.heading: Itemset Support
9639.content:
Itemset support is the fraction of transactions that contain the entire itemset. It normalizes the [[Support Count]] by the number of transactions.

A support threshold defines which patterns are frequent enough to retain. High support indicates prevalence, not that the items are causally connected.

9641.title: Item Adoption

9642.title: Item Adoption
9642.heading: Item Adoption
9642.content:
Item adoption occurs when a user accepts or acts on content received through a social network, such as reading, sharing, retweeting, or applying a label. Adoption can be represented as a positive user-item link, with rejection represented separately when observed.

Its probability can depend on item semantics, the receiver's history, the sender, and the social tie. Adoption therefore serves as both a behavior to explain and a signal for later recommendations.

An IT department acting as a cloud service broker curates available services, negotiates or oversees provider relationships, integrates capabilities, and helps business units choose approved offerings. Its focus moves from owning every system to governing a service portfolio.

9648.title: Isotropic and Anisotropic Thermal Conductivity
9648.heading: Isotropic and Anisotropic Thermal Conductivity
9648.content:
An isotropic material uses the same thermal conductivity in every direction. An anisotropic material requires directional values, so conductive heat flux need not align simply with a scalar conductivity times the temperature gradient.

Transversely isotropic materials share properties within a plane but differ normal to it, while orthotropic materials have three distinct values along orthogonal axes. Rolled sheet and layered structures therefore require orientation-aware inputs in [[Finite Element Thermal Modeling|finite-element models]].

9651.heading: Isosceles Triangle Theorem
9651.content: The isosceles triangle theorem states that angles opposite equal sides are equal. Its converse states that equal angles have equal opposite sides. A proof can bisect the vertex angle to construct two congruent triangles, making the equality of the base angles a consequence of corresponding parts.

An isoparametric quadrilateral element uses the same shape functions to map element geometry and interpolate field variables. Natural coordinates describe a regular parent element that is transformed into the physical quadrilateral.

Higher-order versions add side nodes and can represent curved boundaries. The mapping lets a common formulation handle a range of element shapes while numerical integration evaluates transformed coefficients.

An isometric tile map arranges diamond-shaped tiles so a two-dimensional image suggests a three-dimensional angled view. Grid coordinates must be transformed into slanted screen coordinates rather than mapped directly to horizontal and vertical pixels.

The underlying level can still use a regular tile grid, but rendering order and coordinate conversion must preserve the apparent depth relationship among tiles and objects.

9660.title: Isolating a Variable
9660.heading: Isolating a Variable
9660.content:
Isolating a variable rewrites an equation so the target variable appears alone on one side. The process reverses surrounding operations in an order that preserves equality.

For (3x-5=28), add five to both sides to obtain (3x=33), then divide both sides by three to obtain (x=11). Expressions may first need to be expanded, like terms combined, or denominators cleared. Isolation is an algebraic form of [[Working Backward]]: undo the operations applied to the unknown while applying each change to both sides.

9663.sourceSearchName: isolated speech recognition isolated speech recognition
9663.title: Isolated Speech Recognition
9663.heading: Isolated Speech Recognition
9663.content:
Isolated speech recognition expects separate words or short commands with clear boundaries. Pauses make it easier to segment the signal and compare each utterance with a constrained vocabulary.

Early recognizers often used this mode because it reduced variability. [[Continuous Speech Recognition]] must instead locate word and sound boundaries inside naturally connected speech.

9666.title: ISO Sensitivity
9666.heading: ISO Sensitivity
9666.content:
ISO sensitivity describes the camera's amplification of the sensor signal. Raising ISO allows an image to be exposed with less light, a smaller aperture, or a faster shutter, but it generally makes sensor noise more visible.

An analyst can compare a recorded ISO value with the apparent noise and the other exposure settings. Compression, denoising, resizing, and local image content also affect visible noise, so a mismatch should be interpreted with those transformations in mind.

9669.sourceSearchName: ising model programming ising model programming
9669.title: Ising-Model Programming
9669.heading: Ising-Model Programming
9669.content:
Ising-model programming expresses a problem through variables and interaction coefficients whose energy is minimized by a desirable solution. On a quantum annealer, execution consists of loading those coefficients, allowing the system to evolve, and reading its qubits.

This workflow can feel unfamiliar to programmers trained in control flow. The central design act is the mathematical encoding that connects a domain problem to the machine’s energy states.

9678.title: Irrotational Flow
9678.heading: Irrotational Flow
9678.content:
Irrotational flow has zero curl of the velocity field, meaning fluid particles have negligible local angular velocity. This property permits velocity to be represented as the gradient of a scalar potential.

When the fluid is also ideal and incompressible, the potential satisfies a Laplace-type equation. Irrotationality can hold outside regions where vorticity is generated even though the flow follows curved paths.

9681.title: Irrelevant Ideal
9681.heading: Irrelevant Ideal
9681.content:
For a nonnegatively graded ring generated in degree one, the irrelevant ideal R₊ is the direct sum of all positive-degree components. It is generated by the degree-one part.

Despite its name, it controls projective geometry and graded local behavior. Graded Nakayama arguments reduce a module modulo the homogeneous maximal ideal containing R₊.

9684.heading: Irregular Space-Time Layout
9684.content: An irregular space-time layout contains measured position-time pairs with no shared grid or obvious repeated organization. Locations, times, or both may differ from one observation to the next. STI and [[STIDF Object|STIDF]] represent this form in the `spacetime` package. Analysis and visualization cannot assume a complete array, so observations must be selected or aggregated through their explicit coordinates and time indexes.

9687.title: Irreducible Polynomial
9687.heading: Irreducible Polynomial
9687.content:
An irreducible polynomial is a nonconstant polynomial that cannot be factored into nonconstant polynomials of smaller degree over the chosen coefficient ring or field.

Over a [[Field]], an irreducible polynomial that divides a product divides at least one factor. This prime-like behavior supports the [[Unique Factorization of Polynomials]]. Irreducibility always depends on the coefficient domain.

The source connects irreducibility to maximal principal ideals in K[x]. Quotienting by the ideal generated by an irreducible polynomial produces a field in which the coset of x acts as a root.

9689.title: Irreducible Ideal

9690.title: Irreducible Ideal
9690.heading: Irreducible Ideal
9690.content:
An irreducible ideal is an [[Ideal]] I that cannot be written as I = I₁ ∩ I₂ with both I₁ and I₂ strictly larger than I. Any such intersection forces one component to equal I.

In a [[Noetherian Ring]], every ideal is a finite intersection of irreducible ideals. The source uses this finiteness as a step toward [[Primary Decomposition of Ideals]].

9693.title: Irrational Number
9693.heading: Irrational Number
9693.content:
An irrational number is a real number that cannot be expressed as a quotient of two [[Integer]]s. Its decimal expansion is infinite and nonrepeating.

For example, (sqrt{2}) is irrational, so any finite calculator display of it is an approximation rather than an exact equality. The same distinction applies to (pi): values such as (3.14) or (22/7) can be close, but they are not equal to it. Rational and irrational numbers together form the [[Real Number]]s.

9696.title: IQueryable
9696.heading: IQueryable
9696.content:
`IQueryable` represents a query whose operations can be composed before the data is retrieved. Filtering, sorting, counting, skipping, and taking can be assembled into one expression that the database provider translates and executes.

Deferred execution is important for [[Server-Side Paging]]: the application should narrow the query before materializing its results. Executing too early moves work and excess data into application memory.

9711.title: IP Packet Fragmentation
9711.heading: IP Packet Fragmentation
9711.content:
IP packet fragmentation divides a packet so it can cross a link whose maximum transmission size is smaller than the original packet. The fragments carry enough identification and position information for the destination to reconstruct the original packet.

IPv4 permits routers to fragment packets in transit. IPv6 moves fragmentation responsibility to the sending host, reducing work required from intermediate routers and making path constraints an endpoint concern.

9714.title: Ionospheric GPS Delay
9714.heading: Ionospheric GPS Delay
9714.content: Ionospheric GPS delay occurs because charged particles change the propagation speed of radio signals passing through the upper atmosphere. The effect varies with frequency, time, location, and solar activity, so an uncorrected pseudorange is longer than the geometric path. Dual-frequency receivers estimate the delay by comparing signals that crossed nearly the same path at different frequencies, while single-frequency users depend more heavily on broadcast or augmentation models.

9717.title: Ionizing Radiation
9717.heading: Ionizing Radiation
9717.content: Ionizing radiation transfers enough energy to remove electrons from atoms or molecules. Alpha particles ionize densely but penetrate weakly, beta particles have intermediate behavior, and gamma rays penetrate strongly while interacting less frequently. Biological risk depends on absorbed energy, radiation type, tissue sensitivity, exposure route, and time.

9720.title: IObserver Interface
9720.heading: IObserver Interface
9720.content: `IObserver<T>` is the consumer side of .NET's observable contract. An observer receives value notifications and terminal error or completion signals from a subscribed provider. In the inventory example, product observers register with an observable recorder and react when product data changes. The subscription relationship lets the provider publish without hard-coding each consumer's behavior.

9723.heading: Invisible Function Return
9723.content:
An invisible function return provides a value without automatically printing it at the console. It suits functions whose main visible effect is a plot or message while still allowing assignment of a useful result.

The hidden display behavior should be documented because the value remains available to callers.

9726.title: Inviscid Flow
9726.heading: Inviscid Flow
9726.content:
Inviscid flow neglects viscosity and the associated frictional shear effects. It is an idealization rather than a property of a real fluid, but it can describe regimes where viscous effects are not the focus.

Combined with incompressibility and irrotationality, the assumption leads to potential flow. Boundaries are then enforced through normal-velocity or potential conditions rather than no-slip viscous behavior.
